prose_title: Sir Isaac Newton – The Ingenious Scientist
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
prose_text_en: Sir Isaac Newton was born on Christmas Day, 1642, in Woolsthorpe, England. Raised by his grandmother, he displayed early mechanical ingenuity, creating a water-clock, a sun-dial, and a working model of a windmill. As an adult, he moved from constructing toys to studying the universe, discovering the nature of light and the law of gravitation. Despite his immense intellect and being knighted, he remained humble, famously remarking: 'I seem to myself like a child, playing on the sea-shore, and picking up here and there a curious shell or a pretty pebble, while the boundless ocean of Truth lies undiscovered before me.' He died in 1727 at the age of 85.
summary_en: This biographical narrative explores the life of Sir Isaac Newton, tracing his journey from an inventive child creating mechanical models to a world-renowned scientist. It highlights his discovery of universal laws like gravity and light while emphasizing his profound humility despite his vast knowledge. The text portrays him as a lifelong seeker of truth who viewed his own achievements as insignificant compared to the mysteries of the universe.
